changes.reason: Raising the edge from 1.6 to 2.0 eV improved the RMS from 25.5 to 22.2 meV. Going to 3.0 eV freezes the full d manifold (top at 2.59 eV) and the low part of the s band past the 2 eV comparison limit; capacity allows up to 6.73 eV.

diagnosis: The subspace and the gauge both converge, and every structural check passes. The only check still failing is the model-window RMS of 25.5 meV against a 20 meV limit. The frozen-window edge is the knob that has been moving this number. With dis_froz_max at E_F+1.6 eV the RMS was 1293 meV (ladder point 9). At E_F+2.0 eV it was 22.2 meV. Setting it back to 1.6 eV gave 25.5 meV. So freezing more of the spectrum is what improves the result, and it has not yet gone far enough. The compared states reach E_F+2 eV, but the d bands (DFT bands 7–9) continue up to 2.59 eV. A 2.0 eV edge leaves the top of the d manifold, and the s-like band 10 starting at 1.64 eV, unconstrained right at the edge of the compared range. Moving the edge to E_F+3.0 eV freezes the whole d manifold and the lower part of band 10. That pins the subspace above the comparison limit, so states at or just below 2 eV are no longer at the frozen edge. Capacity holds: at most 6 frozen states at the worst k-point against 6 functions, and the edge can go up to 6.73 eV before it overfills. The next band up (band 11) starts at about 7.8 eV, so nothing outside the target is frozen.
